args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0, the latest release that was healthy in production, and it's passing health checks again. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks, and 18% of requests were erroring.
- **Rollback:** I rolled it back to v2.3.0 in all three regions. v2.2.9 was also healthy, but it's older.
- **After:** All regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, what I rolled back and the health check results afterwards. It also lists follow-ups.

v2.3.1 had never been healthy anywhere before it reached production. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging. Under our policy, deploying a version like that needs approval from the change manager. INC-0001 asks for two things: find out what broke v2.3.1, and check whether that approval was given.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
